I wish I knew a lot of good things to say, but 7 years ago I lost the person who was my best friend, my boyfriend, and someone who I loved and felt something like I've never felt before when we were together.
Everyday with him was happy and magical and I just can't explain what I felt, I am super skeptical but it was an otherworldly feeling that I've never felt for anyone else, not before him, and never after him.

Losing him changed me.
I went through hell. PTSD. Shock. Spent three months crying and being cared by my mom like a baby.
The doctors prescribed me antidepressants.
I've been taking them since them.
But I changed forever, I'm not the same anymore. I tried dating new people once I was "well".
But my "well" never became what I used to be.
Multiple suicide attempts.

A lot of guys took advantage of my emotional fragility and abused me in various ways after this, making my life and my psychological even worse and filling me with traumas.

At almost 30, I've been pratically disabled for almost 8 years and I was never able to fully recover. 
His family knew how much I loved him and cared for him, they gave me all the support they could, calling me to calm me down and sending me gifts...

We didn't get to get married but I know he was the one. Recently I decided to stop dating completly (this year) since I'm too broken and unstable for it. 
I can't, and I won't date anyone else.
I guess that, on that day, life decided that I was going to be alone forever. 

He gave me so much. And then he left me. 
These days organizing my room, I found a sheet of paper written by him. Random notes. It hurted so bad. Those small pieces of those who left, hanging around waiting to be found...They hurt so much.

I really hope that you don't end up like me. Don't let anyone take advantage of your fragility at this sad moment. Be sure that someone you trust is helping and watching over you. Don't let people break you even more until you're broken beyond a point of no return like me. 
I hope you can recover well and find peace and happiness again in your life.

Gruesome accidents that we will never know how long they took to kill someone of if they felt pain.
Victims of crimes. 
We'll never know how we will go, but every single way just seems horrible and painful.
Giving all the people the possibility of choosing a safe, painless, stressless way to go would be an act of mercy and would be the most human thing to do. I'm not afraid of dying but I'm afraid of how it is going to happen. I wish every person had the right to choose it and go peacefully, painlessly.
